transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Ms. Nakamura, do you have a few minutes to talk?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I wanted to come in and discuss your treatment schedule. There was some confusion with the calendar and things didn't go quite right with the timing of your dose yesterday.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It just means there was an issue with the scheduling entries. The dose was administered a bit off from where we intended it to be in the cycle.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Wait. Was it the wrong day?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some instability in the scheduling process. The system didn't align perfectly with the intended cycle date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is that why the nurse asked me so many questions yesterday?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We just had some coordination issues behind the scenes.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Does this change how the medicine works?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're looking that up on your phone. I know it's a lot to take in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just trying to see if the window for immunotherapy is strict.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's a common concern. I can tell you're feeling a bit uneasy about the timing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The most important thing now is that we have a very clear path forward to fix this. Here is exactly what we are going to do. First, I have already consulted with the attending oncologist and the pharmacy lead this morning.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We have recalculated your entire cycle. Your next dose is now rescheduled for Tuesday the 14th at 9:00 AM. That is a firm date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Tuesday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yes. To make sure this doesn't happen again, I have personally entered your dates into a secondary tracking sheet that is taped to the medication cabinet, and the head nurse has verified it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I see.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: From your side, I'd like you to keep a log of the dates you receive the infusions. If you see a date on your paperwork that doesn't match the 21-day cycle we discussed, I want you to flag it to me immediately during rounds.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can do that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will also be sending you a printed copy of the revised calendar before you leave today so you have a hard copy to reference.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thanks.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be back in about an hour to give you that paper and check your vitals. Does that timeline work for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good. I'll see you shortly then.

H.justification: Resident allows the patient to finish all turns, does not interrupt, and uses no rushing language.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and vague hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'confusion with the calendar', 'instability in the scheduling process') without explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the calendar' and 'the system'.

R.justification: Resident names a specific emotion ('uneasy') and engages the patient's emotional bid regarding the phone search.

T.justification: Resident provides specific next steps with timelines (Tuesday 14th, 9 AM), a named patient role (keeping a log), and prevention measures (secondary tracking sheet).
